# EveryWare UI

The UI component library of SDV EveryWare: Figma component sets (one per role, Material 3 names), Rust state machines (everyware_ui_core), the binding to the harry UI framework (everyware_ui), used by harry apps on embedded devices (no Android framework).

This file is the entry for a program. Everything it points to is a source: nothing under docs/ in git is generated.

## Principles
1. One truth, one direction: Action → state → UI model → pixels. Nothing on the screen writes back: a tap is an action like a message from a bundle, so a frame is a function of the state, testable on the host.
2. Figma decides how it looks, code decides what happens: Geometry, colours, variants and names come from the .fig; which variant shows, what a tap does and the data come from Rust. Figma's Play prototype is for people looking at the design: harry never reads it.
3. Names are the contract: A #name on a Figma layer is a field in ui_model.rs. Rename both or neither: everyware_ui_test fails when they drift apart.
4. Components are state machines, owned by the library: Pressed, value, focus, variant and transition live in everyware_ui_core. The app routes a gesture by name and acts on the event, so a button behaves the same in every EveryWare app.
5. A component on a screen is a slot: A named frame with a preview instance inside; harry clones the chosen variant into it. One component, many places, each with its own texts and values.
6. Variants for rare changes, parts for smooth ones: A variant change rebuilds the node (~50 ms on the RB3): kind, disabled, selected. Pressed, fades, thumbs and carets are opacities and meters, display-only, every frame.
7. One spec, two readers: components.json names the sets, their variants and transitions. The Figma generator and the Rust library read the same file, so they cannot disagree.
8. Roles, not contexts: A component is named by its role (button, list item, tile: Material 3), never by what the app puts in it. A new need extends a property or a part before a new component is made.

## Read next
- docs/content/index.md: how a component lives in Figma, the spec and the code; one tap in six stages
- docs/content/rules.md: the rules every harry app with this library follows
- docs/content/<component>.md: one component: its role, how to put it in Figma, the traps; its front matter names the Rust file
- docs/examples/<component>.rs: the code an app writes for it (state, UI model, presenter, the gesture's arm, sending the event on), compiled and run by everyware_ui_recipes_test
- components.json: the sets, their properties and values, the transitions
- the Rust file its guide's front matter names (`rust:`): the state machine and its API with /// docs; harry/src/slot.rs: the parts the code sets (impl Slotted)
- skills/new-app/SKILL.md, skills/use-component/SKILL.md, skills/ui-component/SKILL.md and traps.md, skills/harry-app/SKILL.md: the tasks
- docs/site/ (built by `node docs/build-docs.js`, not in git): the same, rendered for people with previews and a tap simulation

## Components
- #button: A tappable text button, Material 3's filled, tonal and text button, in two widths. (docs/content/button.md, example docs/examples/button.rs)
- #icon-button: A tappable button with one glyph and no label, Material 3's icon button, in two sizes. (docs/content/icon_button.md, example docs/examples/icon_button.rs)
- #toggle: An on/off switch, Material 3's switch: the value moves the thumb and fades the track, the variant is only the state. (docs/content/toggle.md, example docs/examples/toggle.rs)
- #radio: A group of radio buttons where one option is on; the group owns the selection, each button is a variant. (docs/content/radio.md, example docs/examples/radio.rs)
- #dropdown: A closed pill that opens a list of items below it; the open list and the selected item are opacities, the variant only the state. (docs/content/dropdown.md, example docs/examples/dropdown.rs)
- #list-item: One row of a list, Material 3's list item, with a leading icon or image, a headline, supporting text and a trailing end; rows live in a ListView. (docs/content/list_item.md, example docs/examples/list_item.rs)
- #scrollbar: The thumb of a scrolling list: a vertical progress marker along a track, faded in while the list moves. (docs/content/scrollbar.md, example docs/examples/scrollbar.rs)
- #icon: A 24 px glyph (Lucide) for the slots of other components; display only, no state. (docs/content/icon.md, example docs/examples/icon.rs)
- #segmented: One choice of two to four, Material 3's segmented button: the segments are tap targets, the selected one is lit by opacity. (docs/content/segmented.md, example docs/examples/segmented.rs)
- #tabs: The screen's navigation, Material 3's tabs: the chosen tab is lit by opacity, a tap switches the screen with the screens' effect. (docs/content/tabs.md, example docs/examples/tabs.rs)
- Pages (code): Pages that take turns in one place without tabs: one page deeper slides in, Back slides it out, with the screens' effect. (docs/content/pages.md, example docs/examples/pages.rs)
- #tile: A device's card, Material 3's card for a smart home device: a symbol, a title, a subtitle, a value and the device's control; a tap on the card opens the device, the control inside changes it. (docs/content/tile.md, example docs/examples/tile.rs)
- #skeleton: a placeholder while content loads (Material's skeleton loader): grey shapes where the content will be, a heading bar, four text lines or a 16:9 picture, 440 or 832 wide (wide: a side panel's 880 content less 24 on each side) (docs/content/skeleton.md, example docs/examples/skeleton.rs)
- #symbol: The tile of a room's or a device's symbol: 48 px, the soft accent background, one glyph in ink; display only. (docs/content/symbol.md, example docs/examples/symbol.rs)
- #keyboard: The on-screen keyboard: rows of keys with a character each, pressed keys fade a layer; one component, not a set. (docs/content/keyboard.md, example docs/examples/keyboard.rs)
- #slider: A horizontal slider: the fill and the thumb are meters the code moves, the variant is only the state. (docs/content/slider.md, example docs/examples/slider.rs)
- #bar-chart: A row of 24 bars, each with a level and an accent; display only. The app decides what a bar stands for. (docs/content/bar_chart.md, example docs/examples/bar_chart.rs)
- <app>-sheet: The state machine of anything shown over the screen: closed or open, with the open and close transitions; the base of Sheet and Form. (docs/content/overlay.md, example docs/examples/overlay.rs)
- <app>-sheet: A sheet with input fields: a tap focuses a field, the screen's keyboard dock opens and types into it, Enter submits. (docs/content/form.md, example docs/examples/form.rs)
- #keyboard-dock: The screen's one keyboard: an overlay at the bottom with the keyboard component in its slot, open while a field has the focus. (docs/content/keyboard_dock.md, example docs/examples/keyboard_dock.rs)
- #input-field: A one-line text field: the focus ring, the caret and the placeholder are opacities, the variant is only the state. (docs/content/input_field.md, example docs/examples/input_field.rs)
- #sheet: The container for anything over the screen, Material 3's dialog and side sheet, with the app's content component in its slot. (docs/content/sheet.md, example docs/examples/sheet.rs)
